explanation:
[EFFECT]
The hour of the day has a strongly non-monotonic, two-peaked effect on predicted bike demand. Demand is heavily suppressed in the early morning hours (roughly midnight to 6 a.m.), reaching its lowest point around 4–5 a.m. It then surges to a first peak at 8 a.m. (morning commute), dips slightly through midday, and climbs again to its highest point around 5 p.m. (16–17, evening commute), before gradually declining through the late evening.

[IMPORTANCE]
Hour of the day is the single most important feature in the model, ranked 1st out of 9, with an importance score of 0.889. It has by far the greatest influence on predicted demand, dwarfing all other features.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Staffing and bike availability should be concentrated around the two daily peaks — the 8 a.m. morning rush and the 5 p.m. evening rush — while minimal resources are needed in the pre-dawn hours (roughly 1–5 a.m.) when demand is at its lowest.
